title: A high-throughput genetic screening protocol to measure lipid bilayer stress-induced unfolded protein response in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
protocol: Freshly grow the query strains IRE1 and IRE1ΔLD from frozen glycerol stocks.
Streak out the query strains on YPD agar plates containing 200 μg/mL Hyg and incubate at 30°C for 2–3 days.
Inoculate a single colony into 5 mL of YPD liquid medium and incubate at 30°C for 2 days using a culture rotator (40 rpm).
Evenly spread 800 μL of each saturated liquid culture onto a single-well YPD agar plate to prepare the query strain lawns.
Repeat and prepare a total of thirteen query strain lawns for a genome-wide screen with thirteen condensed 384-density format deletion arrays.
Allow the lawns to dry and incubate at 30°C for 2 days.
Mate query strains with the gene deletion arrays.
Mate the query strain containing UPR sensors with yeast deletion library strains on YPD agar plates.
Transfer successfully mated diploid strains onto enriched sporulation agar plates for sporulation.
Select MATa meiotic haploid progeny on SD-His/Arg/Lys/Ura/Met agar plates containing canavanine/thialysine.
Select KanR meiotic haploid progeny on SDMSG-His/Arg/Lys/Ura/Met agar plates containing canavanine/thialysine/G418.
Select KanR (xxxΔ) and HygR (IRE1 or IRE1ΔLD) haploids with the same media as in previous step, supplemented with Hyg.
Pin the query strain from the lawn onto fresh single-well YPD agar plates using the 384 Solid Pin Multi-Blot Replicator.
Pin the 384-density deletion library on top of the query strain.
Incubate at approximately 22°C for 1 day.
Punch out colonies and pin them onto single-well YPD agar plates containing G418/Hyg.
Incubate the plates at 30°C for 2 days.
Punch out selected diploids and pin them onto single-well enriched sporulation agar plates.
Incubate the plates at 22°C for 7 days.
Pin spores from sporulated cultures onto single-well SD-His/Arg/Lys/Ura/Met agar plates containing canavanine/thialysine.
Incubate the plates at 30°C for 2 days.
Punch out MATa meiotic haploid progenies and pin them onto single-well SDMSG-His/Arg/Lys/Ura/Met agar plates containing canavanine/thialysine/G418 solid medium.
Incubate the plates at 30°C for 2 days.
Pin selected haploids onto single-well SDMSG-His/Arg/Lys/Ura/Met agar plates containing canavanine/thialysine/G418/Hyg.
Incubate the plates at 30°C for 2 days.
Inoculate haploid progenies from the 384-density format arrays into four 96 well plates.
Prefill each well with 200 μL of YPD liquid media.
Grow cell cultures for 12–16 hours at 30°C to reach saturation.
Dilute the cell cultures to a density of 0.05 OD/mL using a multi-channel pipette while maintaining a volume of 200 μL per well.
Incubate diluted cells for 4.5 hours at 30°C.
Measure the fluorescence levels of GFP and mCherry reporters from each well with an automated high-throughput sampler (HTS) connected to the LSRFortessa X-20.
Resuspend the cells using a multi-channel pipette before reading with the flow cytometer to prevent clogging.
Acquire cells at low speed, exciting GFP and mCherry at 488 and 561 nm respectively.
Collect GFP fluorescence through a 530/30 band pass filter and mCherry fluorescence through a 610/20 band pass filter.
One 96-well plate is read within 5 minutes, with 10,000 cells per well being measured.
Acquire data in .fcs file format using FACSDiVA v 8.0 software.
Read files with the software FlowJo 10.8.0.
Gate the density plot of recorded events to include intact or viable cells but not ruptured or dead cells for flow cytometry analysis.
Replot the gated population in another density plot and define gate 2 to isolate single cells.
Include only the gate 2 subpopulation in subsequent fluorescence quantification.
Display the fluorescent activity of mCherry (constitutive reporter) and GFP (inducible UPR reporter) in the gate 2 subpopulation for each treatment condition.
Normalize the median of the GFP signal to the median of mCherry to determine relative UPR activity.
Calculate the GFP/mCherry ratio signal for each mutant strain using Microsoft Excel.
Calculate the median of GFP/mCherry ratio signal for each plate (GFPmedian/mCherrymedian).
Calculate the UPR reporter level of each mutant strain using Equation 1.
Exclude knockout candidates with cell counts of 350 cells/well or less from analysis.
Grow selected strains in 500 μL of YPD media to a cell density up to an absorbance of 0.4 OD/mL.
Store selected strains at -80°C as glycerol stocks until ready for further steps.
Measure relative GFP fluorescence using the LSRFortessa X-20 flow cytometer by exciting GFP and mCherry at 488 nm and 561 nm, respectively.
Collect data through a 530/30 band pass filter for GFP and a 610/20 band pass filter for mCherry.
Place cells on slides coated with 1 mg/mL ConA mounted onto Attofluor cell chambers.
Image cells using a Zeiss LSM 710 confocal microscope with a 100× 1.4 NA oil plan-Apochromat objective.
